_comment: The file to edit. words.csv holds the test data and is meant to stay put.
_models: Either {"use": "<name from catalog.json>"} or {"hf": "owner/repo:File.gguf"}. 'owner/repo' on its own picks that repo's Q4_K_M off the HuggingFace API. Missing files download on first use. `python bench.py --catalog` lists the known ones.

prompts.name: P1 shipped
prompts._why: What LlmPrompts.translation sends today. Keep this in step with the app - it is the baseline every other prompt is judged against.
prompts.system: Translate the {from} word into {to}. Reply with only the {to} translation, all in lower case, using the infinitive form for verbs and keeping the article for nouns.

prompts.name: P2 dictionary role
prompts._why: Role alone, no shape rules. Best meaning of anything tried (68/80) and worst exact (30/80) - the clearest example of a prompt problem rather than a model one.
prompts.system: You are a {from} to {to} dictionary. Reply only with the most direct {to} translation.

prompts.name: P2d target anchor
prompts._why: Best overall challenger to P1 so far (64/80 against 65). Restating the target language last fixes the model answering in the wrong language, but costs a word elsewhere.
prompts.system: Translate the {from} word into {to}. Reply with only the {to} translation, all in lower case, using the infinitive form for verbs and keeping the article for nouns. The answer must be a {to} word, never a {from} word.

prompts.name: P2f both clauses
prompts._why: Best German-target prompt found (es-de 12/20 against P1's 11) at the cost of one point overall. Worth it if German lists matter most.
prompts.system: Translate the {from} word into {to}. Reply with only the {to} translation, all in lower case except words that {to} always capitalises, using the infinitive form for verbs and keeping the article for nouns. The answer must be a {to} word, never a {from} word.

_rejected: Tried against P1 (65/80 exact on lfm2-1.2b) and worse, so removed: mid-sentence casing 47, lowercase-unless-required 56, capital-exception 62, shorter-combined 61, and P1 plus a trailing exception 60 - that last one held de-en exactly and collapsed es-de meaning from 14/20 to 7/20. Every wording that touches capitalisation other than 'all in lower case' loses more on the lower-case targets than it gains on German.
